title: School board discusses annual budget - NewsBreak
text:
By JILL ZIMA BORSKI ,
4 hours ago
MARATHON — Holding the line on expenses and a modest tax increase for homesteaded properties were the outcome of the annual budget discussion Tuesday, Sept. 9, at a Monroe County School Board meeting at Marathon High School.
Finance Director Dr. Charlene White provided an overview of the district’s property values and millage rates compared to the previous year. She said the 2025-2026 increase would result in an additional $82 in property taxes for a home valued at $500,000 based on a millage rate of 2.947 ($294.70 in property taxes for every $100,000 of taxable property value) compared to last year’s millage rate of 2.864 ($286.40 for every $100,000).
School board member Dr. Sue Woltanski clarified $500,000 is commonly used because it reflects a common appraised value of a home in Monroe County, accounting for homestead property tax caps.
The only increase in the proposed budget was for employee compensation; all other expenditures remained consistent with the previous year, said White.
The total proposed district expenditure is about $320.65 million, which is $13.28 million higher than the current year’s budget. The general fund, which supports operations, is about $172.4 million and the capital projects fund is $86.9 million, equating to about 27% of the budget.
Woltasnki asked about reserve funds, and White said the district aims to have $10 million on hand but the current balance is $9.6 million.
Monroe County School District sets the expectation of a “students first” focus in the allocation of resources, with a target of 75% of all operating funds going toward classroom/instructional expenditures, according to budget documents.
The board also approved the school year calendar for 2026-2027. Students are to start Aug. 12, with the semester ending Dec. 20. Students return from the break on Jan. 5, and the end of school is set for May 28.
During Great Educational Moments, Caden Pitcher, a junior at Marathon High School, was recognized for earning a perfect score on the math portion of the Scholastic Aptitude Test, and Lillian Wiley and Cindy Augustin, also MHS juniors, were recognized for participating in the Special Olympics Florida Youth Activation Committee and for attending a conference in Orlando.
During public comment, Marathon resident Luis Gonzalez requested field improvements including synthetic turf at MHS. He said in the past rain disrupted and prematurely ended a ball game, which prevented the local team’s opportunity to go to the playoffs, and that more storage and seating is needed at the site as well.
The school district meets next on Oct. 7 at 5 p.m. at Key West City Hall.
